name: sor_backfill_observations
description: Replay a historical system-of-record export (JSONL, one raw record per line, in S3) into sor.observation for an already-registered adapter, using that adapter's human-authored mapping. Runs as an out-of-band Lambda rather than inside the MCP server, so a multi-minute backfill does not hold the MCP server's database connection pool. The insert is idempotent on (adapter_id, dedup_key), so re-running a backfill, or overlapping one with a live poll, cannot double-count observations -- which matters because the drift detectors compute rates over counted rows. Returns what landed; it does NOT return a job id and does not poll.

engagement_id.description: The engagement whose adapter to backfill (uuid).

adapter_key.description: sor.adapter.adapter_key, e.g. 'jira-prod'. The adapter must already be registered: its mapping is the measurement instrument, and it is authored by a human at onboarding (docs/08 section 2.5), never supplied per call.

s3_uri.description: s3://bucket/key of the JSONL export. Exports too large for one 15-minute run are split into several objects and this tool is invoked once per object.

dry_run.description: Run the full mapping and hashing path and report what would land, without writing any observation or touching the adapter's watermark. Use this to check a freshly authored mapping against real records.
